name: Andaz Amsterdam, Prinsengracht
positioning: Andaz Amsterdam Prinsengracht: a design hotel by Marcel Wanders set within Amsterdam's former public library on the UNESCO-listed Prinsengracht canal
best_for: Design lovers who want Marcel Wanders' playful take on Dutch heritage
Travelers who want a canal-side base in central Amsterdam to explore by bike or tram

facts.text: The hotel is set within Amsterdam's former public library.
The hotel was designed by Dutch designer Marcel Wanders.
The hotel is on the UNESCO-listed Prinsengracht canal in Amsterdam-Centrum.
Rooms look out over the Prinsengracht canal, the Secret Garden or the observatorium-inspired atrium.
Rooms feature tulip-inspired chairs and walls with Delftware-like blue and white tiles.
Rooms include a complimentary minibar with non-alcoholic beverages, beer and local snacks.
Renvy is a chef-led restaurant by Randy Karman.
Prins & Aap holds a daily Jenever Hour, a tasting of two Dutch jenevers with a brief history of the spirit.
The hotel has a 24-hour fitness center.
Through the Very Important Dog program, dogs receive a Cloud7 dog bed and blanket, designer bowls and bottled mineral water.
Guest bicycles are available for exploring Amsterdam, and the Prinsengracht tram stop gives convenient access to the Van Gogh Museum and the Rijksmuseum.

highlights.text: The Prinsengracht Suite is the hotel's signature penthouse, with a kitchenette, a private library/study and Marcel Wanders' signature soap bar bathtub.
The hotel's vintage saloon boat offers 60 or 90 minute canal cruises with private dining, departing right in front of the hotel.
One room type has a private terrace overlooking the Secret Garden.
There is no reception desk; staff greet guests and escort them to standing desks in the lobby for check-in.

considerations.text: Guest rooms have an open-concept bathroom with a walk-in shower.
Parking is limited throughout the hotel's Canal District neighborhood.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the hotel's luxury positioning.
